Paragraph 1: Dad opened the box and a sweet little dog appeared. Poppy jumped with joy at the sight of the little dog. She lowered her head to watch it curiously. Then she became so excited that she accidentally knocked over the box in an attempt to get closer. With the box tipping over, out came the little one, who was not shy and instantly got familiar with Poppy. It didn't take long before the two played around the house, cheerfully running after each other.

Paragraph 2: A few weeks later, the boy arrived home from university. He had been missing his parents and the dog since it was the first time that he had been away from home for such a long time. When the boy caught sight of Poppy, he went rushing toward the dog and bent down to give her a big hug. Suddenly, the boy noticed the little dog. "Oh my, who is this?" His parents laughed at the look of surprise on his face. "It's Poppy's new companion," said Mom.

paragraphs.text: I never knew anyone who’d grown up in Jackson without being afraid of Mrs. Calloway, our librarian. She ran Jackson’s Carnegie Library absolutely by herself. SILENCE in big black letters was on signs hung everywhere. If she thought you were dressed improperly, she sent you straight back home to change your clothes. I was willing; I would do anything to read.

My mother was not afraid of Mrs. Calloway. She wished me to have my own library card to check out books for myself. She took me in to introduce me. “Eudora is nine years old and has my permission to read any book she wants from the shelves, children or adults,” Mother said.

Mrs. Calloway made her own rules about books. You could not take back a book to the library on the same day you’d taken it out; it made no difference to her that you’d read every word in it and needed another to start. You could take out two books at a time and two only. So two by two, I read library books as fast as I could go, rushing them home in the basket of my bicycle. From the minute I reached our house, I started to read. I knew this was extreme happiness, knew it at the time.

My mother shared this feeling of mine. Now, I think of her as reading so much of the time while doing something else. I remember her reading a magazine while taking the part of the Wolf in a game of “Little Red Riding Hood” with my brother’s two daughters. She’d just look up at the right time, long enough to answer – in character – “The better to eat you with, my dear,” and go back to her place in the magazine article.
Milwaukee, Wisconsin, is road testing a new way to keep winter roads ice-free by spreading on them cheese brine, the salty liquid used to make soft cheeses, like mozzarella.

Wisconsin, also called “America’s Dairyland,” is famous for its cheese. The state produced 8 billion pounds of cheese last year! As a result, there was a lot of leftover cheese brine. Disposing of (处置) the brine can be expensive. So what should cheese makers do with the waste?

Normally, towns use rock salt to de-ice streets. The salt lowers water’s freezing point, causing ice to melt (融化) . But using cheese brine could help both cheese producers and cities save money, while keeping roads safe. Cheese brine has salt in it, which, like the rock salt, helps lower water’s freezing point.
In addition to saving money, cheese brine could also be a more eco-friendly option. Many people suspect that all the rock salt used every winter is harming the environment.

Rock salt is made of sodium chloride, the same compound (化合物) in ordinary table salt. Sounds harmless, right? But while you probably add only a small amount of salt to your food, road crews spread about 20 million tons of salt on U. S. roads every year!

The chemical washes off roads and goes into the ground. There it can pollute drinking water, harm plants, and eat away soil. By spreading cheese brine on streets before adding a layer of rock salt, Milwaukee may be able to cut its rock salt use by 30 percent.

Cheese brine has a downside too – a smell similar to that of bad milk. “I don’t really mind it,” Emil Norby told Modern Farmer magazine. He works for one of Wisconsin’s county highway commissions and came up with the idea of using cheese brine. “Our roads smell like Wisconsin!” he said.

Today’s world is not an easy adjustment for young adults. A key skill set for success is persistence (毅力) , a characteristic that researchers say is heavily influenced by fathers. Researchers from Brigham Young University discovered that fathers are in a unique position to help their adolescent children learn persistence.

BYU professors Laura PadillaWalker and Randal Day arrived at these findings after following 325 American families over several years. And over time, the persistence gained through fathers led to higher achievement in school.

“There are relatively few studies that stress the unique role of fathers,” PadillaWalker said. “This research also helps to prove that characteristics such as persistence – which can be taught – are key to a child’s life success.”

Researchers determined that dads need to practice an “authoritative” parenting style. Authoritative parenting is not authoritarian: rigid, demanding or controlling. Rather, an authoritative parenting style includes some of the following characteristics: children feel warmth and love from their father; responsibility and the reasons behind rules are stressed; children are given an appropriate level of autonomy (自主权) .

In the study, about 52 percent of the dads exhibited aboveaverage levels of authoritative parenting. A key finding is that over time, children raised by an authoritative father were significantly more likely to develop persistence, which leads to better outcomes in school.

This particular study examined 11 to 14-year-olds living in two-parent homes. Yet the researchers suggest that single parents still may play a role in teaching the benefits of persistence, which is an avenue of future research.

paragraphs.text: Let’s take a minute to think about the water we use. The human body is 60% water and we need to drink lots of water to be healthy. When we are thirsty we just go to the kitchen and fill a glass with clean water.

__31__   For example, farmers, who produce the food we eat, use water to make the plants grow. When we turn on a light or switch on a TV or a computer we use energy and we need water to produce this energy.

The truth is that we are lucky enough to have clean water whenever we want, but this is not the case for many people around the world. __32__   That’s around one in 10 people in the world. If we drink dirty water, we can catch diseases from the bacteria and become ill. Every year over 500,000 children die from diarrhoea (腹泻) from dirty water. That’s around 1,400 children every day! Also, in some countries children walk many kilometres every day to get water. __33__   Therefore, they don’t have time to learn how to read or write and don’t get an education.

__34__   On this day every year, countries around the world hold events to educate people about the problems of dirty water and that clean water is something that everyone should have around the world. At one school in the U. K., children between the ages of 10 and 15 walk 6km with six litres of water. __35__   People give them money to do this and all the money helps get clean water to as many people as possible around the world.

假定你是李华，你校将举办外国学生中文演讲比赛，请给你的英国朋友George写封邮件邀请他参加。内容包括：
(1)比赛时间；
(2)演讲话题；

(3)报名方式。
 注意：
(1)词数80左右；

阅读下面短文，根据所给情节进行续写，使之构成一个完整的故事。

“I’m going to miss you so much. Poppy ,” said the tall, thin teenager. He bent down to hug his old friend goodbye. He stood up, hugged his parents , and smiled, trying not to let his emotions (情绪) get the better of him.

His parents were not quite able to keep theirs under control. They had driven their son several hours out of town to the university where he would soon be living and studying. It was time to say goodbye for now at least. The family hugged and smiled through misty eyes and then laughed.

The boy lifted the last bag onto his shoulder, and flashed a bright smile. “I guess this is it,” he said. “I’ll see you back home in a month, okay?” His parents nodded, and they watched as he walked out of sight into the crowds of hundreds of students and parents. The boy’s mother turned to the dog , “Okay, Poppy, time to go back home.”

The house seemed quiet as a tomb without the boy living there. All that week, Poppy didn’t seem interested in her dinner, her favorite toy, or even in her daily walk. Her owners were sad too, but they knew their son would be back to visit. Poppy didn’t.

They offered the dog some of her favorite peanut butter treats. They even let her sit on the sofa, but the old girl just wasn’t her usual cheerful self. Her owners started to get worried. “What should we do to cheer Poppy up?” asked Dad. “We’ve tried everything.”
“I have an idea, but it might be a little crazy,” smiled Mom. “Without anybody left in the house but us, this place could use a bit of fun. Let’s get a little dog for Poppy.”

It didn’t take long before they walked through the front door carrying a big box . Poppy welcomed them home as usual, but when she saw the box, she stopped. She put her nose on it. Her tail began wagging (摆动) ever so slowly, then faster as she caught the smell.

group-zj-2020-jan-reading-a.overview: 本文是作家 Eudora Welty 的童年回忆散文，回忆她九岁时在 Jackson 的 Carnegie 图书馆借书读书的经历，刻画了严厉的图书管理员 Mrs. Calloway、支持她阅读的母亲，以及作者本人对阅读痴迷的“极度幸福”。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按人物与情境展开：先写令人畏惧的图书管理员及其严苛规矩，再写母亲带“我”办借书证、母亲不畏惧她，接着写在严苛借书规则下“我”如饥似渴地读书的幸福，最后写母亲同样热爱阅读、随时随地手不释卷。

paragraphs.summary: 介绍图书管理员 Mrs. Calloway：她独自管理图书馆，到处挂着“SILENCE”的牌子，衣着不得体就被赶回家换衣服；而“我”为了读书甘愿照做。
paragraphs.function: 引入核心人物并通过具体细节奠定其严厉形象，同时点出“我”对阅读的强烈渴望。

paragraphs.summary: 母亲不怕 Mrs. Calloway，带“我”去办自己的借书证，并当面声明允许九岁的 Eudora 借阅任何书籍（儿童或成人）。
paragraphs.function: 通过母亲的态度与对比，凸显母亲对“我”阅读自由的支持。

paragraphs.summary: Mrs. Calloway 自定借书规矩：当天借的书当天不能还、每次只能借两本；“我”于是每次两本、飞快地骑车把书带回家，一到家就开始读，深感这是极度的幸福。
paragraphs.function: 进一步刻画规则之严，并直接抒发“我”读书时“极度幸福”的核心情感。

paragraphs.summary: 母亲与“我”共有这份对阅读的热爱：她常一边做别的事一边读书，连陪孙女玩“小红帽”扮大灰狼时也手不释卷，只在该接话时抬头应一句又回到杂志里。
paragraphs.function: 呼应并升华“我”的阅读之爱，说明这种对阅读的痴迷是母女共有的，收束全文。

group-zj-2020-jan-reading-b.overview: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍美国威斯康星州密尔沃基市用奶酪盐水（cheese brine）替代部分岩盐（rock salt）来给冬季道路除冰的新办法。文章从该做法的提出讲起，依次说明其工作原理（含盐降低水的冰点）、双重经济效益（既帮奶酪厂处理废料又帮城市省钱）、环保优势（减少岩盐对环境的污染），并以这一做法的小缺点（气味）收尾。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文按"引入新做法→背景与废料问题→工作原理→经济与环保益处→污染机理与减量效果→缺点"的顺序展开，先说明现象再分析利弊，结构清晰，由果及因再到评价。

paragraphs.summary: 密尔沃基市正在试验用奶酪盐水（制作软奶酪时产生的咸味液体）撒在路面上来防止冬季道路结冰。
paragraphs.function: 开篇引入文章主题——用奶酪盐水给道路除冰这一新做法。

paragraphs.summary: 威斯康星州盛产奶酪，去年产了80亿磅，因而剩下大量奶酪盐水，而处置这些废料代价高昂，引出奶酪厂该如何处理废料的问题。
paragraphs.function: 交代背景，说明大量奶酪盐水废料及其处置难题，为新做法的提出铺垫。

paragraphs.summary: 通常城镇用岩盐除冰，盐降低水的冰点使冰融化；奶酪盐水中也含盐，同样能降低冰点，因此既能让奶酪厂和城市省钱又能保证道路安全。
paragraphs.function: 说明除冰的工作原理，并指出奶酪盐水与岩盐一样含盐、可降冰点，是新做法的科学依据。

paragraphs.summary: 除了省钱，奶酪盐水还可能是更环保的选择，因为很多人怀疑每年冬天大量使用的岩盐正在危害环境。
paragraphs.function: 承上启下，从省钱转向环保益处，提出岩盐危害环境的疑虑。

paragraphs.summary: 岩盐的成分是氯化钠，与食盐相同，看似无害，但路政部门每年在美国道路上撒约2000万吨盐，用量极大。
paragraphs.function: 通过对比食盐用量与道路用盐量，说明岩盐用量巨大，暗示其潜在危害。

paragraphs.summary: 这些化学物质冲入地下，会污染饮用水、危害植物、侵蚀土壤；而先撒奶酪盐水再撒岩盐，密尔沃基有望减少30%的岩盐用量。
paragraphs.function: 具体说明岩盐对环境的危害机理，并给出新做法可减少岩盐用量的量化效果。

paragraphs.summary: 奶酪盐水也有缺点——气味像变质牛奶；但提出该想法的Emil Norby并不介意，还打趣说路面闻起来"有威斯康星味"。
paragraphs.function: 指出新做法的缺点并以当事人的乐观态度收尾，使说明全面客观。

group-zj-2020-jan-reading-c.overview: 本文是一篇说明文，介绍杨百翰大学（BYU）研究者的一项研究发现：父亲在帮助青少年子女培养毅力（persistence）方面具有独特作用，而毅力又与更好的学业成就相关。文章进一步解释了有助于培养毅力的“权威型”（authoritative）教养方式的特征，并指出未来研究可关注单亲家庭。

discourseStructure.summary: 全文先提出核心发现（父亲对培养子女毅力有独特作用），再交代研究规模与结果，引用研究者原话强调父亲角色的独特性，接着解释“权威型”教养方式的具体特征及其与毅力的关系，最后指出研究对象局限并提出未来研究方向。

paragraphs.summary: 指出毅力是年轻人成功的关键技能，而毅力深受父亲影响；BYU 研究者发现父亲在帮助青少年子女培养毅力上处于独特位置。
paragraphs.function: 引出话题并提出研究的核心发现

paragraphs.summary: 介绍两位 BYU 教授在追踪 325 个美国家庭数年后得出结论：通过父亲获得的毅力会带来更高的学业成就。
paragraphs.function: 交代研究方法、样本与主要结果

paragraphs.summary: 引用 Padilla-Walker 的话，强调专门研究父亲独特作用的研究很少，并指出毅力等可被教导的特质是孩子人生成功的关键。
paragraphs.function: 用研究者原话强调研究的独特价值

paragraphs.summary: 说明父亲需要采用“权威型”教养方式：它不同于专制（authoritarian）的严苛、苛求与控制，而是让孩子感到温暖与爱、强调责任与规则背后的原因、给予孩子适度自主权。
paragraphs.function: 界定并解释“权威型”教养方式的特征

paragraphs.summary: 研究中约 52% 的父亲表现出高于平均水平的权威型教养；由权威型父亲抚养的孩子随时间推移更可能培养出毅力，从而在学校取得更好结果。
paragraphs.function: 用数据佐证权威型教养与毅力、学业结果的关系

paragraphs.summary: 指出本研究只考察生活在双亲家庭的 11 至 14 岁孩子，但研究者认为单亲家长仍可能在传授毅力方面发挥作用，这是未来研究的方向。
paragraphs.function: 说明研究局限并提出未来研究方向

q-zj-2020-jan-021.questionFocus: 考查对 Mrs. Calloway 人物形象的概括，需根据第一、三段对其行为与规矩的细节归纳其性格特征。

locationParaphrases.note: 开篇即以 I … grown up in Jackson 的第一人称回顾个人成长往事，与 autobiography（自传）回忆自身经历的体裁吻合。

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 它旨在提高孩子的学业成就。

trap.sourceQuote: the persistence gained through fathers led to higher achievement in school
trap.optionText: It aimed to improve kids' achievement in school.
trap.explanation: 原文把“更高的学业成就”表述为研究观察到的结果（led to higher achievement），而选项把它说成研究的目的（aimed to improve），混淆了“研究发现的结果”与“研究的目标”，且题目问的是研究的“独特之处”，提高学业成就并非其独特性所在。

trapEvidence.quote: the persistence gained through fathers led to higher achievement in school
trapEvidence.anchor: 通过父亲获得的毅力带来更高学业成就

locationParaphrases.targetText: There are relatively few studies that stress the unique role of fathers
locationParaphrases.note: 题干 special about（特别之处）对应原文 the unique role of fathers 以及 relatively few studies 所体现的“独特/罕见”，即研究的独特之处在于聚焦父亲的作用。
正确项 fathers' role in parenting 是原文 the unique role of fathers 的同义改写。

q-zj-2020-jan-028.questionFocus: 考查“权威型”父亲在教养子女时的具体做法，需定位第四段对 authoritative parenting 特征的列举。
q-zj-2020-jan-028.stemTranslationZh: 一位权威型父亲在抚养子女时会怎么做？

trap.claim: An authoritative father would ignore their demands.
trap.explanation: 原文未提及权威型父亲会“无视孩子的要求（ignore their demands）”。文中 demanding 一词是用来描述被否定的“专制型（authoritarian）”父亲，与“无视要求”意思无关，故该说法原文未提及。

trap.sourceQuote: children are given an appropriate level of autonomy (自主权)
trap.sourceHighlight: given an appropriate level of autonomy
trap.explanation: 原文说权威型父亲给予孩子“适度的自主权”，即让孩子自己做决定；选项“替他们做决定”与之方向相反，属于黑白颠倒。

trapEvidence.quote: children are given an appropriate level of autonomy (自主权)
trapEvidence.anchor: 给予孩子适度自主权

trap.sourceQuote: Authoritative parenting is not authoritarian: rigid, demanding or controlling.
trap.explanation: 原文明确指出权威型教养“不是”专制型——不严苛、不苛求、不控制（controlling）；选项却说权威型父亲会“控制他们的行为”，恰好与原文相反，且借用了原文 controlling 一词，属黑白颠倒。

trapEvidence.quote: Authoritative parenting is not authoritarian: rigid, demanding or controlling.
trapEvidence.anchor: 权威型不等于专制（控制）型

evidence.quote: responsibility and the reasons behind rules are stressed

locationParaphrases.targetText: the reasons behind rules are stressed
locationParaphrases.note: 正确项 Explain the rules（解释规则）对应原文 the reasons behind rules are stressed（强调规则背后的原因），讲清规则缘由即是向孩子解释规则。

q-zj-2020-jan-029.questionFocus: 考查研究者指出的未来研究可关注的群体，需定位末段关于 future research 的表述。
q-zj-2020-jan-029.stemTranslationZh: 根据研究者的说法，哪一群体可以成为未来研究的关注点？

evidence.quote: single parents still may play a role in teaching the benefits of persistence, which is an avenue of future research
evidence.anchor: 单亲家长是未来研究方向

trap.sourceText: This particular study examined 11 to 14-year-olds living in two-parent homes.
trap.relationNote: 原文 11 to 14-year-olds 指的是“本次研究已经考察”的对象，而非“未来研究”的对象；选项借这一年龄段的原文词钩误导，把已研究群体当成未来研究群体。

trapEvidence.quote: This particular study examined 11 to 14-year-olds living in two-parent homes.
trapEvidence.anchor: 本研究已考察 11–14 岁孩子

trap.claim: Authoritarian fathers can be a focus of future studies.
trap.explanation: 文中 authoritarian（专制型）只是用来与 authoritative（权威型）作对比说明，原文从未提及把“专制型父亲”作为未来研究的关注对象，属无中生有。

trap.claim: Mothers in two-parent homes can be a focus of future studies.
trap.explanation: 原文虽提到 two-parent homes，但只是说明本研究对象生活在双亲家庭，并未提出把“双亲家庭中的母亲”作为未来研究方向；该群体在未来研究语境中原文未提及。

locationParaphrases.targetText: which is an avenue of future research
locationParaphrases.note: 题干 future studies 与原文 an avenue of future research 对应，是定位答案句的关键线索。

locationParaphrases.targetText: single parents still may play a role in teaching the benefits of persistence
locationParaphrases.note: 正确项 Single parents 直接对应原文 single parents，并被研究者点名为未来研究（future research）的方向。

q-zj-2020-jan-030.questionFocus: 考查全文最佳标题，需概括文章核心主旨——父亲（尤其是权威型父亲）有助于孩子培养毅力。
q-zj-2020-jan-030.stemTranslationZh: 下列哪一项是本文最佳标题？

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 权威型父亲的三个特征

trap.sourceQuote: an authoritative parenting style includes some of the following characteristics: children feel warmth and love from their father; responsibility and the reasons behind rules are stressed; children are given an appropriate level of autonomy (自主权)
trap.sourceHighlight: an authoritative parenting style includes some of the following characteristics
trap.explanation: 权威型父亲的特征仅是第四段的局部内容，不能概括全文主旨；以此作标题以偏概全、范围过窄，遗漏了文章关于父亲帮助孩子培养毅力这一核心。

trapEvidence.quote: an authoritative parenting style includes some of the following characteristics
trapEvidence.anchor: 权威型教养的特征只是局部内容

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 年轻人未来成功的关键技能

trap.sourceQuote: A key skill set for success is persistence (毅力)
trap.sourceHighlight: A key skill set for success
trap.optionText: Key Skills for Young Adults to Succeed in Future
trap.explanation: 文章只聚焦“毅力”这一种关键技能，且重点在于父亲如何帮助孩子培养毅力；选项用复数 Key Skills 泛指多种技能，范围过宽，且偏离了“父亲作用”这一核心。

trapEvidence.quote: A key skill set for success is persistence (毅力)
trapEvidence.anchor: 关键技能特指毅力

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 孩子往往从父亲那里学会坚毅

evidence.quote: fathers are in a unique position to help their adolescent children learn persistence
evidence.anchor: 父亲帮助孩子培养毅力（核心主旨）

evidence.quote: a characteristic that researchers say is heavily influenced by fathers

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.optionTranslationZh: 家庭关系影响学业表现

trap.sourceQuote: the persistence gained through fathers led to higher achievement in school
trap.explanation: 文章讲的是“父亲帮助培养毅力、进而带来更好学业表现”，主语是父亲与毅力；选项用宽泛的 Family Relationship（家庭关系）取代“父亲/毅力”，范围过大且偏离主旨，同时忽略了核心环节“毅力”。

trapEvidence.quote: children raised by an authoritative father were significantly more likely to develop persistence, which leads to better outcomes in school
trapEvidence.anchor: 经由父亲培养毅力才带来学业改善

locationParaphrases.sourceText: Children Tend to Learn Determination from Father
locationParaphrases.targetText: fathers are in a unique position to help their adolescent children learn persistence
locationParaphrases.note: 正确标题中 learn Determination from Father 对应原文 help their adolescent children learn persistence，其中 Determination 与 persistence（毅力/坚毅）同义，准确概括全文主旨。
